Basic Concepts of Cellular Energetics and Metabolism
• Cellular Energetics
• Processes that a cell obtains, transforms, applies energy.
• These may include:
• Exergonic chemical reactions that release energy
• And endergonic chemical reactions that consume energy
• All these reactions are collectively known as metabolism
• Metabolism
• Sum total of all biochemical reactions occuring in cell

Basic Concepts of Cellular Energetics and Metabolism
• Cellular Energetics
• Processes that a cell obtains, transforms, applies energy.
• These may include:
• Exergonic chemical reactions that release energy
• And endergonic chemical reactions that consume energy
• All these reactions are collectively known as metabolism
• Metabolism
• Sum total of all biochemical reactions occuring in cell

Basic Concepts of Cellular Energetics and Metabolism
• Metabolic reactions are divided into
• Anabolism
• Reactions that use smaller molecules to build larger molecule. E.g. using amino acids to make protein
• Cellular energy is used in these processes.
• Catabolism
• Reactions that break down complex molecules to simple molecules
• Cellular energy is produced in these processes.
• Cellular respiration is a group of catabolic reactions that food fuels (E.g. glucose) are broken down to produce ce

Nature and Functions of Enzymes • Factors that affect enzyme activity • (1) Temperature • When temperature is low, enzymes are inactive. Low enzyme activity leads to low reaction rate. When temperature increases, higher enzyme activity leads to higher reaction rate. • Maximal reaction rate is reached when temperature increases to optimum temperature (37-40˚C for most human enzymes). • When temperature increases furtherly, enzyme molecules are denatured to decrease enzyme activities. Reaction rat

Nature and Functions of Enzymes
• Factors that affect enzyme activity
• (1) Temperature
• When temperature is low, enzymes are inactive. Low enzyme activity leads to low reaction rate. When temperature increases, higher enzyme activity leads to higher reaction rate.
• Maximal reaction rate is reached when temperature increases to optimum temperature (37-40˚C for most human enzymes).

Nature and Functions of Enzymes • Factors that affect enzyme activity • (2) pH level • Most enzymes work within narrow range of pH level (optimum pH). • Extreme pH levels (Too alkaline or too acidic) lead to denaturation of enzymes and thus low enzyme activity and low reaction rate.

Concepts of Homeostasis • (1) Negative feedback mechanism • Most homeostatic control methods are negative feedback mechanisms. • In these methods, outputs (responses) are opposite with the inputs (original stimuli). • Therefore, the outputs (responses) reduce the inputs (original stimuli) to keep within normal range.

Concepts of Homeostasis
• (1) Negative feedback mechanism
• Most homeostatic control methods are negative feedback mechanisms.
• In these methods, outputs (responses) are opposite with the inputs (original stimuli).
• Therefore, the outputs (responses) reduce the inputs (original stimuli) to keep within normal range.
